subject: Vanguard: request for SLO carveout and latency commitment evaluation
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@vanguardtech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@vanguardtech.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: 99.5% 1s latency commitment for search use-case

Marissa / Soojin,

Thanks for the call this morning. As mentioned, Vanguard is planning a phased rollout of Redwood for our customer-facing search index. Performance is a hard requirement for our compliance and customer SLA reporting. We'd like to formalize the following as part of the contract: a 99.5% 1s p95 latency commitment for text generation calls at our expected QPS (~120 req/s) with a monthly uptime credit if the commitment is missed.

I attached a short SLO request doc with traffic shape and retention needs. Procurement would like an internal assessment of feasibility and any carveouts (maintenance windows, regional failover) before we proceed to legal. Please advise on timeline — we need a proposal by EOD Friday (Dec 4) to stay on the vendor selection cadence.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Platform Engineering
Vanguard Technologies
Attachment: vanguard-slo-request.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: 99.5% 1s latency commitment for search use-case

Looping you in, Soojin — Vanguard is asking for a tighter p95 than our standard public SLOs and a credit structure. They’re a strategic target account (high expansion potential). Can we get engineering/product to validate feasibility at ~120 QPS (documents attached)? They want a proposal by EOD Dec 4.

Quick context: current public guidance is 95% < 1s p95 for hosted tier; Dedicated customers often have bespoke SLAs but this is tighter and includes uptime credit language.

Thanks — I can push for a short sync with the customer if helpful.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: vanguard-slo-request.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Vanguard SLO request — need product/infra evaluation

Team — Vanguard has asked for a 99.5% 1s p95 at ~120 QPS and wants a credit if missed. We need a short feasibility note by EOD Dec 4 covering:
- Can runtime meet 1s p95 at that QPS on a Dedicated cluster profile? Any required config (batching, KV cache warm-up)?
- What are reasonable carveouts (maintenance, regional failover, force-majors)?
- If we can’t hit 99.5% p95, what alternative commit can we reliably sign (e.g., 99% p95, or 99.5% p95 for a limited window)?
- Any infra cost / capacity asks and preliminary pricing impact.

Karthik / Ben — can you run a targeted perf estimate/quick perf run (use perf-run-20261130.csv for context) and propose an ops-safe carveout language? Laura — flag anything legal/finance that needs pre-approval (credits/terms) so we can scope the ask before sending to procurement.

I’ll own the account communication and consolidate responses.

—Soojin
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Vanguard SLO request — perf estimate and carveouts

Soojin — quick findings from infra/product:
- Based on model family and traffic shape (short prompts, avg tokens=48) the runtime can target ~120 QPS on a 6-GPU Dedicated pool with tuned batching and persistent KV cache. See attached perf run summary.
- 1s p95 at that QPS is aggressive but achievable under steady-state provided: warm caches, request shaping for spikes above 160 QPS, and a dedicated regional capacity reservation.
- Recommended carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (2x/month, 30m each), operational degradation during cold-start for first 2 hours after full cluster restart, and force-majeure. Also recommend an explicit traffic spike policy: latency SLO applies when 95% of 15-minute intervals are below 160 QPS; above that threshold we apply best-effort and no credit.
- Cost impact: estimated incremental infra delta ~+24% over standard dedicated pricing to reserve cushion and on-call burn for guaranteed SLAs.

I’ll draft proposed SLO language for ops to review. If product wants to accept 99.5% p95 only for a limited (pilot) window, say first 3 months, that lowers cushion needs.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Attachment: perf-run-20261130.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@vanguardtech.com>, Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@vanguardtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood proposal: SLO carveout & pilot commitment for Vanguard

Sanjay / Natalie — thanks for your patience while we evaluated the request. Internal stakeholders (product, infra, and finance) reviewed feasibility and proposed the following path forward:  

1) Pilot commitment (90-day): Redwood will commit to a 99.5% p95 <= 1s SLO for your search workload for the initial 90-day pilot, scoped to your agreed traffic profile (avg 120 QPS, token profile provided). During the pilot we require a dedicated regional pool (6 GPUs) and traffic-shaping above 160 QPS.

2) Carveouts/clarifications: the SLO excludes scheduled maintenance (two 30m windows / month), operational cold-starts following full cluster restarts (up to 2h), and force-majeure events. SLO is measured on customer-tagged requests and applies only when 95% of 15-minute intervals are under 160 QPS.

3) Credits/terms: If SLO is missed during pilot, Redwood will provide a service credit up to 10% of that month’s invoice. Any long-term firm commitment beyond pilot will require capacity reservation and a pricing uplift (~+24% estimated).

4) Next steps: if this baseline is acceptable, procurement/legal can route a short amendment. We’ve attached a draft term sheet and perf summary. We can also schedule a 30-minute technical runbook session next week to align on runbook and monitoring.

We want to ensure the commitment is achievable operationally and that your team has clear expectations on when credits apply. Please confirm whether Vanguard can accept the pilot structure by Mon, Dec 7 so we can lock capacity.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-proposed-terms-v2.docx, perf-run-20261130.csv
